texts.summary: Méry de Vic writes after the assassination of Henri III and the accession of Henri IV. The opening cleartext reports the arrival of the news and local allegiances. The cipher reports troops near Limoges and divided loyalties; later cleartext discusses expenses, elections, intercepted dispatches and cannon for rebel forts.
texts.note: Re-read 23 Oct 2026 (b30), still decoded, not read: the letter (Gallica btv1b103164206 views 89-96, ff. 40r-43r) is clear except one 16-line cipher block on f. 43r; no contemporary decipherment, no DECODE record, Lasry's full decryption not in the repository. The block decoded sign by sign on the full-size IIIF image with Lasry's key table (texts/f43r_cipher_decode.tsv): it reproduces both of his excerpts and adds most of the rest (an armed gathering eight leagues from the town, 1,200 foot and 200 horse with two or three guns; 'qui a tousiours parle en ... servit[e]ur de roy se change'; enemies of the [?ligue] taking the pretext of religion; 'ie [?les] contiens ce que ie puis'). Partial reading texts/f43r_reading.md: whole body 0.667 (20/30) with the clear text, but the cipher passage alone 0.308 (4/13), explicit holes 0.462; 7 letters on look-alike alternates, 2 sense-only values flagged (ꝗ = g, Ӿ = le). Blocker: no-key-material (about 12 groups and 4 signs with no value in Lasry's table).
